messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify buffer_compact returns -1 and leaves buffer unchanged if allocation fails.
test_metadata.rationale: Ensures that on allocation failure, the buffer is not modified and the error is reported, which is critical for robust error handling and memory safety.

dependencies.name: buffer_length
dependencies.reason: Used to determine logical length of buffer for allocation

assertions.name: assert_int_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify return value is -1 on allocation failure
assertions.usage: Check that buffer_compact returns error code

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_content
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer content is unchanged after failed compact
assertions.usage: Check buffer data remains the same

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_length
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer string length is unchanged after failed compact
assertions.usage: Check buffer length remains the same

assertions.name: helper_assert_buffer_size
assertions.purpose: Verify buffer allocated size is unchanged after failed compact
assertions.usage: Check buffer size remains the same

utilities.name: helper_create_buffer_with_content
utilities.purpose: Create a buffer with known content for testing
utilities.usage: Setup phase to create test buffer

preconditions: buffer has non-zero length and extra capacity (len > buffer_length(self))
buffer->data and buffer->alloc point to valid memory
setup_requirements.initial_state: A buffer with known content and extra capacity, ready to be compacted.

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to a valid buffer with extra capacity
primary_function_args.rationale: Triggers compact logic; buffer must be valid and have unused space

state_changes: Buffer state before → Buffer state after: no change
invariants_maintained: No memory leaks or double frees

assertions_required.description: Verify buffer_compact returns -1 on allocation failure
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Error not reported on allocation failure

assertions_required.description: Buffer content is unchanged after failed compact
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Buffer content was modified on error

assertions_required.description: Buffer string length is unchanged after failed compact
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Buffer length was modified on error

assertions_required.description: Buffer allocated size is unchanged after failed compact
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Buffer size was modified on error

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All memory allocated for buffer is freed; no leaks.

operation_sequence: Create buffer with known content and extra capacity
Record original content, length, and size
Simulate allocation failure for calloc (see edge_cases_to_note)
Assert buffer content, length, and size are unchanged
edge_cases_to_note: Directly simulating allocation failure is not possible without mocking; this test is only valid if calloc can be forced to fail naturally (e.g., by requesting a huge allocation or running in a constrained environment).
If not possible to force calloc to fail, this test may be skipped or marked as not applicable in environments without allocation failure.

path_coverage_analysis.description: Allocation failure in buffer_compact: calloc returns NULL, function returns -1 and buffer is unchanged.

integration_test_suggestions: Test buffer_compact in a loop with varying buffer sizes to observe behavior under memory pressure.
Test buffer_compact after multiple buffer modifications to ensure no state corruption.
